analysis: What changed versus the Nov 3 9:00 AM brief: the overnight story flipped from 'midterms today, results unknown' to a confirmed Democratic sweep of both chambers, and the market's reaction was a full round trip — Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.4% and S&P 500 futures 1.4% overnight, then recovered to solid gains by ~5:20 AM ET (Dow +1.3%, S&P +0.9%, Nasdaq +0.8%). That whipsaw is the signal: the initial read was 'tougher AI oversight,' the second read is 'divided government plus AI earnings strength.' The AI earnings leg is genuinely strong — AMD, Arista and Super Micro all beat and guided up after the close, with AMD's data-center revenue nearly doubling and a 2027 growth framework above 80% — but the caveats inside AMD's print (client revenue slowing, free cash flow down to $554M, Q4 margin easing to ~55%) keep the 'AI spending pays off' question open rather than settled. Sector rotation is the cleanest premarket tell: clean energy, hospitals and insurers up; defense, prisons and Musk-linked names down — politics, not fundamentals, is driving those moves. Tesla/SpaceX weakness is a political-repricing story (Musk spent hundreds of millions backing losing Republican candidates), not a company disclosure. Signal vs noise: the sweep and the AI beats are signal; the overnight futures plunge that fully reversed is noise in hindsight, though it shows how jumpy positioning is with the Nasdaq-100 already in correction. USAC's Q3 story is unchanged and quiet: the beat held, the call added tightened full-year guidance, and Friday's $0.525 distribution is the next dated item.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Democrats sweep Congress in the midterms — NBC projects Democrats also won the House after earlier Senate projections — and index futures whipsawed overnight: Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.4% and S&P 500 futures 1.4% before reversing; by about 5:20 AM ET, Dow futures were up about 1.3%, S&P 500 futures about 0.9% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.8%, with the dollar index down about 0.5% and gold futures up about 3%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The overnight plunge fully reversing into gains shows the first political read (tougher AI oversight) is competing with the calmer read (divided government, no radical policy shift) — direction into the open is still being negotiated.

headlines.headline: Premarket sector rotation on the sweep (Reuters): clean energy surged — First Solar +9.4%, Sunrun +10%, Enphase +7.6%, NextEra +2.2% — while defense fell (Northrop Grumman -5%, RTX, Lockheed Martin and L3Harris each down over 3%), prison operators dropped (GEO Group -6.7%, CoreCivic -5.2%), data-center operators slipped (Core Scientific -2.8%, Iren -1.4%), and hospitals/insurers rose (HCA +3.7%, Centene +4.5%, Molina +6%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Politics is driving the premarket tape sector by sector — winners map to expected Democratic priorities (clean energy, health spending), losers to Trump-era beneficiaries.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell about 3.6% and SpaceX about 3.2% in premarket trading after Democrats' sweep, including losses for Musk-backed Republican candidates in Texas, where both companies are based; analysts flagged extra congressional scrutiny as a possible drag on a potential Tesla-SpaceX merger, which remains exploratory.
headlines.why_it_matters: A political repricing, not a company disclosure — Musk's hundreds of millions backing losing Republican candidates now reads as policy headwind for his companies.

headlines.headline: AMD beat after the close: Q3 revenue $13.38B (+45% year over year) vs $13.09B expected, adjusted EPS $2.09 vs $1.95 expected, data-center revenue nearly doubling (+97%) to a record $8.55B; Q4 revenue guided to about $17B vs $16.2B expected, and management said it expects 2027 revenue growth above 80%; shares gained 7.7% after hours to $520.99 (Morningstar).
headlines.why_it_matters: The strongest AI-demand evidence yet this week — a beat plus a step-change guide directly answers the 'AI spending slowdown' fear that put the Nasdaq-100 in correction.

headlines.headline: Arista Networks jumped about 13-14% after hours to $192.63 after Q3 revenue rose 58.5% year over year to $3.66B (vs $3.33B expected), its fastest growth since its 2014 IPO, with Q4 guided to $3.9-4.0B revenue.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second AI-infrastructure beat landing the same night as AMD's — the hardware leg of the AI trade is reporting strength, not just promising it.

headlines.headline: Super Micro Computer climbed about 10% after hours to $34.50 after fiscal Q1 revenue rose nearly fourfold to $19.95B (vs $17.35B expected) with adjusted EPS $1.81 vs $1.23 expected, and guided fiscal Q2 sales to $19.5-21.5B; Block rose 6.7% to $81.10 on higher payments profit.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI server story keeps beating on volume — but with gross margin at 12.8%, the question stays whether the growth converts to profit at scale.

headlines.headline: Carried from Tuesday's session: the S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92 and the Nasdaq gained 0.83% to 25,372.01, snapping three-day losing streaks, while the Dow fell 0.38% to 51,786.72 as Apple slid on its December-quarter gross-margin guide (45-46% vs 47.9% in September, rising memory costs cited) despite beating fiscal Q4; Nvidia rebounded about 2.9% and was up about 0.5% in premarket, while hyperscalers (Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) were mostly lower in early premarket trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tuesday's split tape (tech up, Dow down) is the base the premarket is building on — Apple margin pressure versus chip strength is still the unresolved tension.

headlines.headline: Today's calendar: October ISM services index, ADP private payrolls for October and the September trade balance are due, plus the Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement; CVS, Uber and McDonald's report before the open, Qualcomm and Arm after the close; markets also watch for Washington's next decision on the US-Israeli war on Iran.
headlines.why_it_matters: A full macro and earnings slate lands on top of the election repricing — any ADP or ISM surprise will move yields and the futures' fragile recovery.

headlines.headline: Carried, no update: Nvidia reportedly told cloud partners to sell at least 51% of services to non-Chinese companies under future contracts, per the Financial Times; Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied it, existing contracts are exempt, and a follow-up report said the guidance was not being enforced as a mandatory restriction.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile: if confirmed, it caps a China-demand channel for future contracts; if softened, it is noise on top of a chip bounce.
